title: Lemonade Change
statement: Each lemonade costs 5. Customers queue up paying with a 5, 10 or 20 note, and you must give the correct change immediately from notes you have already taken. You start with nothing. Return whether every customer can be served.
constraints: change must be given at the moment of sale, from notes already received
hints: Only the counts of fives and tens matter; a twenty is never useful as change, so there is no need to count them.
A ten needs one five. A twenty needs either a ten and a five, or three fives.

For a twenty, always prefer the ten-and-five combination. Fives are the flexible note - they can pay for a ten as well - so spending three of them when a ten was available is what makes an otherwise servable queue fail.

cases.name: first customer pays with a ten
fives spent too freely on the first twenty
